issues.legal_issue: An issue finally decided in one of two separate suits between the same parties cannot be reopened in a second appeal arising from the other suit when the decision in the first suit was not appealed.
material_facts: The parties brought two separate suits that raised the same question of an easement for the flow of water for fishing purposes.
The issue was directly and substantially in issue in the suit brought by the respondents and was decided against them by the District Court.
The respondents did not appeal the District Court’s decision in their suit, so it became final.
The respondents’ second appeal concerned the decree in the appellant’s separate suit; the District Court had disposed of appeals from both suits in a common judgment.
issues.conclusion: The fishing-easement issue was barred by res judicata and could not be decided again in the second appeal arising from the other suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, including Explanation I, bars trial of an issue directly and substantially in issue between the same parties when it has been heard and finally decided in a former suit; a suit decided earlier is a former suit even if instituted later, provided its decision preceded the decision in the suit under consideration. Under Sheodan Singh v. Smt. Daryao Kunwar, decisions in separate suits on common issues can operate as res judicata in one another; Badri Narayan Singh v. Kamdeo Prasad Singh confirms that a common appellate judgment may embody separate decisions. Narhari v. Shanker was distinguished because it concerned one suit, not separate suits.

rule.if: separate_suits_between_same_parties and same_issue_directly_and_substantially_in_both and issue_finally_decided_in_one_suit and decision_not_appealed_in_that_suit and second_appeal_arises_from_other_suit

predicates.separate_suits_between_same_parties: The same parties litigated the matter in two separate suits.
predicates.same_issue_directly_and_substantially_in: The same issue was directly and substantially in dispute in each suit.
predicates.issue_finally_decided_in_one_suit: A court heard and finally decided the issue in one of the suits before the second appeal was decided.
predicates.decision_not_appealed_in_that_suit: The party against whom the decision was made did not appeal the decision in that suit.
predicates.second_appeal_arises_from_other_suit: The proceeding is a second appeal arising from the other of the two suits.

issues.definition: When the same issue between the same parties is finally decided in one of two separate suits and that decision is not appealed, the issue cannot be reopened in a second appeal arising from the other suit.

issues.legal_issue: A party may challenge an interlocutory ruling in an appeal from the final decision even though the party did not appeal the interlocutory ruling when it was made.
material_facts: In a remand judgment, the High Court rejected the appellant’s contention that the issue was barred by res judicata.
The appellant did not appeal the remand judgment.
After the proceedings on remand, the High Court issued a final judgment, which the appellant appealed and in which the appellant again challenged the earlier ruling.
issues.conclusion: The failure to appeal the remand judgment did not prevent the appellant from challenging its ruling in the appeal from the final judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Under Satyadhyan Ghosal v. Smt. Deorajin Debi, an interlocutory order may be challenged in an appeal from the final decree or order, whether no appeal lay from the interlocutory order or an available appeal was not taken.

predicates.appeal_from_final_decision: The proceeding is an appeal from a final judgment, decree, or order.
predicates.earlier_interlocutory_ruling_not_appeale: A party did not appeal an earlier interlocutory ruling, whether because no appeal lay or because no appeal was taken.
predicates.party_challenges_earlier_ruling_in_final: In the appeal from the final decision, a party challenges the correctness of the earlier interlocutory ruling.

issues.definition: When a party appeals from a final decision, the party may challenge an earlier interlocutory ruling that was not separately appealed.
